Mexican soldiers and federal prosecutors arrested two alleged members of the Cártel del Noreste in Nuevo Laredo on Sunday, including a man federal authorities describe as a regional operator for the group and his son, who is accused of leading a hitman cell, according to PorEsto.

Troops from the Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional and the Fiscalía General de la República detained Gerardo Javier “N,” known as “La Pocha,” and his son, known as “El Nazi,” during an operation in which authorities carried out three search warrants at the same time, federal Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch announced. Agents from the Agencia de Investigación Criminal and the Fiscalía Especializada en materia de Delincuencia Organizada took part in the operation.

Investigators allege “La Pocha” was a regional operator for the Cártel del Noreste in eastern Nuevo Laredo and link him to the production and sale of synthetic drugs, homicides, kidnappings and extortion, according to the reports. He faces an arrest warrant in Mexico and an extradition process to the United States, where he is wanted on drug conspiracy and trafficking charges, and he is also accused of involvement in the disappearance of victims’ bodies, an activity investigators say began during his time with Los Zetas and continued with the Cártel del Noreste.

His son, “El Nazi,” is identified by investigators as the alleged head of a hitman cell known as “Las Tropas del Infierno,” an operative arm of the Cártel del Noreste, according to PorEsto.

The arrests were announced Sunday morning. Authorities had not released further details about formal charges or court appearances as of publication. The men are accused, not convicted, and are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Sources: PorEsto, November 8, 2026; El Congresista, November 8, 2026.

title: Alleged Cártel del Noreste figures “La Pocha” and “El Nazi” arrested in Nuevo Laredo
